The face-up cards, on the three signed-off questions

The face-up arcana-mfh lander answering the same three questions the signed-off face-down deck answers. One deck of three visible cards, three ad headlines, swapped by a single URL parameter. Every stage below was screenshotted by an automated flow test against a muted sandbox, with the real chat transcript it produced.

Why there was nothing to build: the face-up decode-him deck already existed and was live. The headline is keyed by hook, not by deck, so a face-up lander on ?hook=cards-honest renders the identical headline string the face-down deck did — no code change was needed to reuse the signed-off headlines. What this run does is prove that, and it surfaced two copy lines that needed fixing.

Compliance: every read stays a tendency, never a verdict — it reads him as a leaning and hands the authority back to her intuition, and never states as fact that he is lying, that he will return, or how he feels. No exclamation marks; no flat verdicts. Asserted, not just reviewed.

Two copy fixes this run found

1 · A line that predicted a return — arcana-mfh / cards-return / the Fool

The 28 Jul sign-off deliberately rewrote this beat to be conditional. The face-down deck got the new wording; the face-up deck was never given it, so the deck about to run ads presupposed that he comes back.

was — “…it leans toward a fresh, unexpected turn; what comes back often comes back as a new beginning, not the old shape.” now — “…it points to a road still open rather than a door closed; if something does come of this, it begins fresh rather than picking up where it broke.”

2 · A rejected accusation still live — arcana-eef / cards-honest / the Fool

The second face-up deck still carried the accusation the sign-off rejected. Now matches the approved wording. Not in this report’s screenshots — arcana-eef is a separate deck — but fixed and pinned by a test.

was — “…it leans toward someone careless with the truth more than cruel with it…” now — “…it points to a man who hasn’t sat down and thought it through; what’s unsaid here may be unexamined rather than hidden…”

Both lines now have a test pinning the approved phrase, so a future edit can’t quietly walk them back — the protection the face-down deck already had, extended to the face-up decks.
